- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.0) or shows strong bearish momentum, model often overshoots early; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent peak.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85% of recent high), model frequently overcorrects downward; apply a 1–2% upward bias to offset mean reversion.  
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.0–0.5), model often fails to adjust for mean reversion; use 3–5 day moving average of true values as baseline.  
- Forecast horizon > 14 days shows persistent lag; add 0.5–1.0% downward adjustment for each day beyond 14.  
- If sentiment history includes multiple negative entries (≥2), model tends to underestimate; add 1–2% upward bias to forecast.
